records.title: LiteFeet / Get Lite Emerged from Harlem and the Bronx
records.summary: LiteFeet, also written Lite Feet and often described as getting lite, is a New York street dance culture connected to Harlem and the Bronx in the early-to-mid 2000s.
records.related_to: LiteFeet origins, Get Lite, Harlem, Bronx

research_details.label: Claim Text
research_details.value: LiteFeet, also written Lite Feet and often described as getting lite, is a New York street dance culture connected to Harlem and the Bronx in the early-to-mid 2000s.

research_details.label: Confidence
research_details.value: High based on multiple public sources, but still open to community context and correction.

research_details.label: Sources to Review
research_details.value: Red Bull Music Academy Daily, Vulture, STEEZY, CBS/Paramount, and academic writing on LiteFeet.

research_details.label: Archive Note
research_details.value: Community members can add details about early dancers, crews, courts, parties, battles, and borough-specific history.

records.title: The 2013 Harlem Shake Meme Is Not the Real Harlem Shake
records.summary: The 2013 viral Harlem Shake meme is not the real Harlem Shake and was criticized by Harlem dancers for disconnecting the name from the actual Harlem dance.
records.related_to: Harlem Shake meme, real Harlem Shake, cultural confusion

research_details.label: Claim Text
research_details.value: The 2013 viral Harlem Shake meme is not the real Harlem Shake and was criticized by Harlem dancers for disconnecting the name from the actual Harlem dance.

research_details.label: Confidence
research_details.value: High based on first-person and media sources.

research_details.label: Sources to Review
research_details.value: Dance Enthusiast interview with Chrybaby Cozie, Wired, and AllHipHop.

research_details.label: Archive Note
research_details.value: This record should preserve the difference between the real Harlem Shake and the internet meme.

records.title: LiteFeet and Subway Showtime Criminalization
records.summary: LiteFeet became strongly associated with subway Showtime performance culture, and public coverage in the mid-2010s connected subway dance policing to broken-windows enforcement, race, class, and public-space politics.
records.related_to: LiteFeet, Showtime, subway dancing, criminalization, public space

research_details.label: Claim Text
research_details.value: LiteFeet became strongly associated with subway Showtime performance culture, and public coverage in the mid-2010s connected subway dance policing to broken-windows enforcement, race, class, and public-space politics.

research_details.label: Confidence
research_details.value: High based on documentary, journalism, and academic sources.

research_details.label: Sources to Review
research_details.value: i-D/Vice, Viewing NYC, The Nation, Katie Beswick academic chapter, and Urban Democracy Lab.

records.title: Get Lite to LiteFeet Music Evolution
records.summary: Public music coverage describes a shift around 2011 where a newer generation of dancers and producers refreshed Get Lite into LiteFeet music by raising tempo, adding layered sound, chants, samples, and call-and-response energy.
records.related_to: Get Lite, LiteFeet music, 107 BPM, producers

research_details.label: Claim Text
research_details.value: Public music coverage describes a shift around 2011 where a newer generation of dancers and producers refreshed Get Lite into LiteFeet music by raising tempo, adding layered sound, chants, samples, and call-and-response energy.

research_details.label: Confidence
research_details.value: Supported by VICE/Noisey source, but specific producer timelines need community verification.
